evals.prompt: We just got back from KubeCon EU in Amsterdam: 412 badge scans and a Google Sheet where our engineers noted about 30 real conversations. The scanner app said 'Scan to get the demo config emailed to you'. Our CMO wants every scan loaded into our 6-email HubSpot nurture by Monday and says GDPR is fine because B2B legitimate interest covers it. Contacts are roughly 40% Germany, 30% rest of EU, 15% UK, 15% US. We sell a Kubernetes cost-monitoring SaaS with a free tier. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: A follow-up plan that refuses the blanket nurture, gates by purpose line and jurisdiction, sends the promised config to every scan, personal notes to A conversations, and measures the cohort.
expectations: States that the nurture sequence must not be sent to all 412 scans
Says legitimate interest does not authorise marketing email in Germany, and in the rest of the EU only where a member-state rule allows it, citing ePrivacy prior consent or EDPB Guidelines 1/2024
Says a scanned badge is not consent for email advertising in Germany (UWG s.7 or equivalent wording)
Sends the demo config to every scanned contact, including those with no conversation notes
Keeps the config email free of promotion or newsletter subscription
Says the scanner's purpose line ('demo config') limits marketing even for UK or US contacts
Sends personal notes to the noted A conversations from the engineer who had the conversation
Sets the A follow-up within about two working days and gives memory of the conversation as the reason, not a lead-response study
Routes to sales only records whose notes show a stated buying need
Recommends loading contacts into the CRM without enrolling them in the nurture unless the gate allows it
Defines an event cohort tag and an activation event to measure at 30, 60 and 90 days
Treats UK contacts with personal or unknown-type addresses as individual subscribers needing consent or soft opt-in
Matches the scans against the CRM so existing customers go to their account owner and earlier unsubscribes win

evals.prompt: Our hackathon sponsorship at HackZurich wrapped Sunday. 61 teams, 23 used our payments API, lots of university students and a few high-schoolers. Our VP Sales wants the SDRs to call every participant this week because 'research shows you have to respond within 5 minutes or the lead dies'. Our recruiter also wants the list. Can you draft the plan and the outreach?
evals.expected_output: A hackathon follow-up that routes students to community, rejects the 5-minute study as evidence, and uses a showcase plus project-specific notes and an activation path.
expectations: Gives participants under 18 no marketing without the privacy owner's sign-off
Routes students or job seekers to community or recruiting, never sales
States the 5-minute lead-response figures came from inbound web-form leads, not event or hackathon contacts
Notes the speed study was co-authored by or tied to a lead-response software vendor (InsideSales)
Publishes a public showcase or recap of submissions, with the teams' permission
Sends personal notes to teams that built on the payments API, referencing their specific project
Includes a day-30 check-in for teams still building
Proposes an activation path or extended credits for the 23 API teams
Hands to sales only participants who stated a buying need
Limits the recruiter's use of participants to those whose capture or reply covers recruiting
Measures the hackathon cohort's activation rather than calls made or emails opened

evals.prompt: I ran a 90-minute hands-on workshop at PyCon US on building retrieval pipelines with our vector DB. 45 people on the roster (sign-up form said 'get the workshop materials'). My plan: send slides + a thank-you, then add everyone to our monthly newsletter. Sound good? I need something to show my boss in 60 days.
evals.expected_output: A workshop follow-up built around an activation path from where the session ended, roster purpose respected, cohort measurement at 30/60.
expectations: Says slides alone end the journey and proposes a finish-the-exercise activation path
Starts the activation path from the step where the workshop ended, or provisions a sandbox or credit
Rejects adding the whole roster to the newsletter because the sign-up said 'get the workshop materials'
Offers an opt-in to the newsletter rather than automatic subscription
Defines an activation event (for example a first successful query or API call) for the cohort
Sets 30-day and 60-day readings against the boss deadline
Recommends tagging the workshop cohort so activations are attributable
Compares the cohort with a non-event baseline or labels any target as self-set
Uses the stuck step of attendees who stall as feedback for the workshop or docs
Offers any newsletter opt-in as a separate choice with no second email unless the attendee clicks
Sends the activation path to roster members whose sign-up covered the materials

evals.prompt: At DevOpsDays Montreal and DevOpsDays Paris we had no scanners, so we ran a draw for a mechanical keyboard: about 150 paper entries with name and work email ('Enter to win - winner announced at closing'; about 40 also ticked a separate 'send me product news' box), plus a few business cards handed to our engineers. Marketing wants to send everyone a 20% discount code. A colleague says CASL lets us use business cards for six months. What's allowed?
evals.expected_output: Raffle entries excluded from marketing; CASL disclosure-based implied consent explained correctly; France B2B rule; business cards treated separately.
expectations: Says raffle entries without the ticked box must not get the discount email
Explains the raffle purpose line covers only the draw
Corrects the six-month claim: the six-month window applies to inquiries, not to a business card disclosure
Explains CASL implied consent from a disclosed address requires relevance to the person's business role
Treats business cards handed to engineers differently from raffle entries
States the French B2B rule requires the person to have been informed at collection and able to object
Recommends a public recap or announcement for raffle entrants instead of email marketing
Keeps the entrants who ticked the separate product-news box eligible for marketing
Recommends agreeing retention with the privacy owner, deleting raffle data once the prize ships
Adds sender identification and an unsubscribe mechanism to any marketing message sent to Canadian contacts

evals.prompt: Our event leads never convert. Last year we did 9 conferences and almost nothing came of it. My CEO read that '80% of trade show leads are never followed up' and wants a 5-email/30-day sequence fired at everyone within 24 hours of each show. We sell an observability platform, PLG with a sales team for enterprise. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that rejects the untraced 80% statistic, looks at capture quality and purpose, proposes tiered tracks and cohort measurement with influenced vs sourced reporting.
expectations: States the '80% of trade-show leads are never followed up' figure has no traceable original study
Diagnoses capture quality (notes, grades, purpose lines) as a likely cause before proposing more emails
Rejects a single 5-email sequence for every contact
Assigns different tracks to A, B and C contacts
Limits B and C contacts to at most one message unless they respond
Proposes a public recap as the track for C contacts
Defines event-cohort activation at 30/60/90 days as the outcome metric
Distinguishes influenced from sourced pipeline and warns against claiming source for influenced deals
Sets a per-batch spam-complaint stop rule instead of waiting for the domain-level 0.10% Postmaster rate to react
Feeds the follow-up results into the per-event sponsorship renew or drop decision
Labels any conversion threshold as self-set or derived from the company's own data, not a published benchmark

evals.prompt: We sponsor the monthly Go meetup in Berlin and the organizer just passed us the sheet people sign at the door ('name + email, for the pizza headcount next time'). We also gave a talk at GopherCon EU and about ten people came up after with questions; one asked for pricing for 200 seats. Now I want to put the sheet into our product newsletter and email the talk folks a demo invite. Thoughts?
evals.expected_output: Germany prior consent; sign-up sheet purpose limits; talk follow-ups as personal answers; the pricing ask as the only sales handoff.
expectations: Says the pizza-headcount sheet cannot be used for the product newsletter
Says Germany requires prior express consent for email advertising, business addresses included
Returns or deletes the pizza-headcount sheet and never emails the people on it
Treats the talk questioners as personal notes delivering the answer owed, not a demo-invite blast
Hands only the 200-seat pricing request to sales
Makes the sales handoff an introduction in the same thread, not a cold sequence
Does not build a mailing list from the talk audience
Offers a newsletter opt-in through a public page or recap rather than by email to non-consented contacts
Says a list handed over without a sponsor-sharing notice gets no import
Tells the user to tell the organizer the sheet was shared without a sponsor-sharing notice
Recommends a suppression list for people who object

evals.prompt: AWS re:Invent wrap-up: 520 scans, the scanner screen said 'Scan to get product updates from Acme'. About 30% of the scans are German, plus some from Brazil and Japan; the rest are US and UK, many UK ones on gmail addresses. As a Diamond sponsor we also got the organizer's opt-in attendee list of 3,000 people. Marketing wants to send our launch announcement to all of it tomorrow from our main domain. How do we do this right?
evals.expected_output: Updates-purpose scans gated by jurisdiction: German double opt-in, US/UK corporate allowed with opt-out, unknown jurisdictions prior-consent, organizer list within its notice, stop rules and CRM import.
expectations: Sends German scans one confirmation email free of promotion and enrols them only on the click (double opt-in)
Allows the launch email to US scans because the purpose line covered updates, with an opt-out and postal address
Treats Brazil and Japan as prior-consent until the privacy owner names the local rule
Treats UK gmail addresses as individual subscribers needing consent or soft opt-in
Mails EU and UK attendees on the organizer list only where their consent named the company, not generic sponsors or partners wording
Loads the records into the CRM as non-marketing contacts and enrols only those the gate allows
Sets a per-batch complaint stop rule before sending
Warns that one mass send from the main domain puts its reputation at risk for later campaigns
Defines an event cohort tag and activation readings at 30, 60 and 90 days
Gates the organizer list as a separate source with its own row, apart from the 520 scans
